subject.title: Telegram retry regex too strict: bare grammy `Network request for 'X' failed!` (no "after") never classified as recoverable for `context: send`, drops outbound messages

question: Should a bare grammY `Network request for 'X' failed!` message without verified nested pre-connect provenance be replayed for non-idempotent Telegram sends, or should OpenClaw keep it single-shot and improve durable visible recovery?
rationale: Source inspection shows this is an intentional duplicate-delivery boundary rather than a mechanical regex omission; accepting the broad message trades message loss against possible duplicate sends and therefore needs an explicit owner decision.

options.title: Require proven pre-connect provenance
options.body: Keep ambiguous envelopes single-shot, propagate concrete low-level causes through wrappers, and add durable visible reconciliation for outcomes that cannot be classified safely.

options.title: Retry every bare envelope once
options.body: Treat the grammY message itself as proof of a pre-connect failure, accepting the risk that a misclassified ambiguous send may produce a duplicate message.

recommendation.title: Require proven pre-connect provenance
recommendation.body: Keep ambiguous envelopes single-shot, propagate concrete low-level causes through wrappers, and add durable visible reconciliation for outcomes that cannot be classified safely.

likelyOwner.reason: The strict classifier and duplicate-safety policy originate in this contributor's merged Telegram retry work.
